description:
Incident bot + diagnostics improvements is a cross-functional reliability initiative to reduce incident MTTR and repeat incidents by upgrading Redwood Inference’s automated incident context gathering. The bot (primarily used in #incidents and #eng-oncall) will be enhanced to automatically attach: (1) recent deploy context (service/version, rollout phase, canary status, related PRs), (2) customer/tenant-safe config diffs (feature flags, routing policy, quota/rate-limit, model pins) with redaction, and (3) saturation signals (GPU utilization, KV cache pressure, queue depth, scheduler/backpressure indicators, regional capacity) plus deep links to dashboards and traces.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-triage and time-to-mitigation for common incident classes (deploy regressions, misconfig, regional capacity/saturation).
- Standardize “first 5 minutes” incident context so on-call has consistent evidence, fewer ad-hoc queries, and better handoffs.
- Improve graceful degradation decisions during incidents by surfacing relevant routing/fallback configuration and capacity signals.

In-scope deliverables:
- Incident bot v2 Slack experience (context “cards”, interactive actions, retries/timeouts, feature flag rollout).
- New/updated backend endpoints/services to export deploy metadata, config diff retrieval with redaction, and telemetry query aggregation with caching/guardrails.
- Observability updates: new metrics for saturation signals, dashboards, and alert tuning aligned to SLOs/error budgets.
- Runbooks/standards for incident context collection and access/audit requirements.

Out of scope:
- Full incident management process overhaul, major status page tooling changes, and long-term data warehouse re-architecture.

Key stakeholders:
- SRE (incident process owner, paging hygiene, MTTR tracking): Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello, Jacob Stein.
- Platform control plane + routing (config/policy, permissions, graceful degradation): Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Jordan Lee.
- Telemetry/observability (signals, dashboards, query performance/cardinality): Logan Wright, Allison Grant, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson.
- Release engineering (deploy metadata, rollout linkage): Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer.
- Product (rollouts/console deep links, success metrics): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes.
- Support/CS (customer-impact feedback loops via Jira): ties to SUP tickets and escalations.

Phases / timeline (typical 6–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + requirements: baseline MTTR, top failure modes, signal inventory, data access constraints.
2) Data-source plumbing: deploy metadata export, config diff API, saturation metrics standardization.
3) Bot UX + reliability: Slack rendering/actions, timeouts/retries, caching, rate limiting, redaction.
4) Rollout: feature-flagged beta in limited on-call rotations/regions, then broad rollout.
5) Measurement: MTTR deltas, “context completeness” score, on-call feedback, follow-up tickets.

Constraints:
- Strict tenant/customer data handling: config diffs must be redacted; access must be audited.
- Telemetry cardinality and query cost must be bounded; bot queries must degrade gracefully.
- Bot must remain usable during partial outages (timeouts, fallback links, cached context).
